indices.name: NDVI
indices.label: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index
indices.sensor_hint: Requires a red and a near-infrared band (Sentinel-2 B04/B08, Landsat 4/5, drone NIR).
indices.notes: Primary index. Unaffected by soil brightness for full canopies, but saturates above ~0.8.

indices.name: NDRE
indices.label: Normalized Difference Red Edge
indices.sensor_hint: Needs a red-edge band (Sentinel-2 B05/B06/B07 or MicaSense RedEdge).
indices.notes: Better than NDVI for mature, dense canopies and chlorophyll content.

indices.name: EVI
indices.label: Enhanced Vegetation Index
indices.sensor_hint: Needs blue, red and NIR bands with reflectance values in 0-1.
indices.notes: Reduces atmospheric and soil noise; expects scaled reflectance, not raw DN.

indices.name: SAVI
indices.label: Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index
indices.notes: Useful on sparse canopies where exposed soil biases NDVI.

indices.name: GNDVI
indices.label: Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index
indices.notes: More sensitive to chlorophyll than NDVI; the usual choice for nitrogen status on a closed canopy.

indices.name: NDMI
indices.label: Normalized Difference Moisture Index
indices.sensor_hint: Needs NIR and SWIR1 (Sentinel-2 B08/B11, Landsat 5/7/8/9).
indices.notes: Canopy water content — separates drought stress from nitrogen stress where NDVI cannot.

indices.name: NDWI
indices.label: Normalized Difference Water Index
indices.notes: Positive over open water and saturated soil; used to find ponding and drainage problems.

indices.name: OSAVI
indices.label: Optimized Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index
indices.notes: Fixed 0.16 soil-brightness correction — the standard soil-adjusted index for agricultural canopies.

indices.name: MSAVI
indices.label: Modified Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index (MSAVI2)
indices.notes: Self-adjusting soil line and later saturation than NDVI — the best default on sparse or patchy emergence.

indices.name: PSRI
indices.label: Plant Senescence Reflectance Index
indices.sensor_hint: Needs red, green and blue bands (any RGB sensor).
indices.notes: Tracks ripening and senescence after NDVI has flattened — useful for harvest timing.

indices.name: CVI
indices.label: Chlorophyll Vegetation Index
indices.sensor_hint: Needs red, green and NIR bands.
indices.notes: Ratiometric in green, so it tolerates uneven illumination across a drone mosaic.

indices.name: RECI
indices.label: Red-Edge Chlorophyll Index
indices.sensor_hint: Needs a red-edge band (Sentinel-2 B05/B06/B07, MicaSense RedEdge).
indices.notes: Stays sensitive in dense canopies where normalised indices saturate.

indices.name: GCI
indices.label: Green Chlorophyll Index
indices.sensor_hint: Needs green and NIR bands — works on ordinary RGB+NIR drone payloads.
indices.notes: The green-band sibling of RECI, for sensors without a red-edge band.

classes.label: Very low vegetation
classes.description: Bare soil, senescent or severely stressed canopy. Very little active green biomass.

classes.label: Low vegetation
classes.description: Sparse or stressed canopy. Often early emergence, poor establishment or localised stress.

classes.label: Moderate vegetation
classes.description: Developing canopy with partial ground cover. Expect a mix of soil and leaf signal.

classes.label: Very healthy vegetation
classes.description: Dense, vigorous canopy at or near full cover for the observed crop stage.

crop_health.note: Thresholds are configurable in config.yaml or per request (thresholds override).

classical.label: Index threshold segmentation
classical.description: Binary mask from a fixed value on a vegetation index or single band.

classical.label: Otsu segmentation
classical.description: Automatic threshold chosen from the image histogram (OpenCV Otsu).

classical.label: Multi-class threshold segmentation
classical.description: Splits the index into ordered classes (bare soil / sparse / moderate / dense) using configurable edges.

classical.label: Connected-component zones
classical.description: Connected-component labelling of an existing mask into discrete zones with areas.

models.label: U-Net (semantic segmentation)
models.loader: torch.load / torch.jit.load of a trained checkpoint
models.notes: Register a loader with register_model('unet', fn) once a trained checkpoint exists.

models.label: DeepLabV3+ (semantic segmentation)
models.install_hint: pip install torch torchvision (CPU wheels are enough)
models.notes: Vibes Lite intentionally does not download pretrained weights automatically.

models.label: YOLO segmentation
models.install_hint: pip install ultralytics (optional, not required by the platform)
models.notes: Suited to per-plant or per-weed detection on drone imagery.

models.label: Custom TorchScript / ONNX model
models.install_hint: pip install torch or onnxruntime when a model is available
models.notes: Use register_model('torchscript', loader) with your exported artifact.

segmentation.note: Classical methods work out of the box. Model-backed methods appear in the registry so a trained U-Net / DeepLab / YOLO-seg checkpoint can be added later without changing the pipeline or the API.

charts.index_map: Continuous vegetation index map with legend
charts.index_overlay: Transparent EPSG:4326 overlay for the web map
charts.histogram: Index value histogram with class boundaries
charts.timeseries: Index over time with trend and healthy-area share
charts.change_map: Diverging change map between two observations

disclaimer: Vibes Lite computes vegetation indices and index-based health classes. These describe canopy greenness and density and are not a diagnosis of crop disease, pest pressure or nutrient deficiency.
